# vk 0.10.0 — `set_*` fluent construction setters

Development release, 2026-11-01. Cargo package **`vkrust 0.10.0+1.4.365`**,
Rust library/import name **`vk`**, Git tag **`v0.10.0`**, MIT licensed.
The `+1.4.365` suffix identifies the unchanged pinned Vulkan header snapshot;
it is not a Vulkan 1.4 driver requirement.

[Developer guide](https://dev.realm.software/vk) ·
[Rust API reference](https://docs.rs/vkrust/latest/vk/) ·
[Realm](https://realm.software/)

## API and migration

This is a minor API release with a **source-breaking, ABI-preserving** rename:
every generated fluent record-construction setter gains a `set_` prefix on its
existing ergonomic name. Pointer-prefix stripping is unchanged, so raw Khronos
prefixes do not re-enter the public spelling:

- `application_info(&info)` → `set_application_info(&info)`
- `queue_create_infos(&queues)` → `set_queue_create_infos(&queues)`
- `enabled_extension_names(&names)` → `set_enabled_extension_names(&names)`

```rust
let application = vk::ApplicationInfo::default()
    .set_application_name(c"vk example")
    .set_api_version(vk::API_VERSION_1_0);
let info = vk::InstanceCreateInfo::default()
    .set_application_info(&application);
```

Method signatures, lifetimes, checked counts and error propagation are
unchanged; migration is a mechanical call-site rename. There are no legacy
aliases for the former names.

Unchanged:

- raw `#[repr(C)]` record fields such as `p_application_info`;
- command, loader, dispatch and allocator APIs;
- typed extension chaining via `push_next` and the sealed `ChainNode`
  internals, including the sealed `set_p_next` trait method;
- the separate StdVideo `set_*` bitfield accessors;
- `AllocationCreateInfo` and other native Rust configuration records, which
  keep struct-literal construction.

`BaseInStructure`/`BaseOutStructure` now carry an inherent `set_p_next` field
setter alongside the sealed `ChainNode::set_p_next` trait method. Rust method
resolution keeps the two distinct; chain construction continues to call the
trait method through its bound.

## Evidence and limits

The release checkpoint passed the workspace test and doctest suite, strict
Clippy and rustfmt, and the generator's `--check` idempotence gate on the
private tree. Release CI reruns the configured tests, package/consumer checks
and pinned-header oracles on this release's exact public snapshot.

No new sanitizer, VMA donor or native-hardware qualification was run for this
delta; the rename changes spelling, not construction semantics, and the
recorded allocator profiles carry forward unchanged — see the
[qualification report](../qualification.md). The allocator remains
Experimental; all existing qualification limits continue to apply. No
production readiness claim follows from this release.
